questions.question_text:
Match the following:
Field
Length in bits
P. UDP Header’s Port Number
I. 48
Q. Ethernet MAC Address
II. 8
R. IPv6 Next Header
III. 32
S. TCP Header’s Sequence Number
IV. 16
questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: UDP port numbers are 16 bits long (P-IV). Ethernet MAC addresses are 48 bits long (Q-I). The IPv6 Next Header field is 8 bits long (R-II). TCP sequence numbers are 32 bits long (S-III). Hence the correct matching is P-IV, Q-I, R-II, S-III.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the slow start phase of the TCP congestion
control algorithm. Note that cwnd stands for the TCP congestion window and MSS denotes
the Maximum Segment Size.
(i) The cwnd increases by 2 MSS on every successful acknowledgment.
(ii) The cwnd approximately doubles on every successful acknowledgement.
(iii) The cwnd increases by 1 MSS every round trip time.
(iv) The cwnd approximately doubles every round trip time.

Which one of the following is correct?
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: In TCP slow start, the congestion window (`cwnd`) increases by 1 MSS for each acknowledged segment. Consequently, when all segments in a flight are acknowledged, `cwnd` approximately doubles every round-trip time (RTT). Thus, statement (iv) is TRUE.
questions.question_text_latex:
Consider the following statements regarding the slow start phase of the TCP congestion control algorithm. Note that $cwnd$ stands for the congestion window size and $MSS$ denotes the Maximum Segment Size.

    \item[(ii)] The $cwnd$ increases by 1 $MSS$ on every successful acknowledgement.
    \item[(iii)] The $cwnd$ increases by 1 $MSS$ every round trip time.
    \item[(iv)] The $cwnd$ approximately doubles every round trip time.
\end{itemize}
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

questions.question_text:
Consider a long-lived TCP session with an end-to-end bandwidth of 1 Gbps (= 109 bits-per-
second). The session starts with a sequence number of 1234. The minimum time (in seconds,
rounded to the closest integer) before this sequence number can be used again is _______.
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: A 32-bit sequence number space contains $2^{32} = 4{,}294{,}967{,}296$ bytes. At a transmission rate of $1\text{ Gbps} = \frac{10^9}{8} = 1.25 \times 10^8\text{ bytes/s}$, the wrap-around time is $\frac{2^{32}}{1.25 \times 10^8} = \frac{4294967296}{125000000} \approx 34.36$ seconds $\approx 34$ seconds.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a 1 Gbps network with an MTU of 1500 bytes and a 32-bit sequence number space. The minimum time (in seconds, rounded to the nearest integer) after which the sequence numbers can wrap around is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

questions.question_text:
Consider an IP packet with a length of 4,500 bytes that includes a 20-byte IPv4 header and
a 40-byte TCP header. The packet is forwarded to an IPv4 router that supports a Maximum
Transmission Unit (MTU) of 600 bytes. Assume that the length of the IP header in all the
outgoing fragments of this packet is 20 bytes. Assume that the fragmentation offset value
stored in the first fragment is 0.

The fragmentation offset value stored in the third fragment is _______.
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: Total payload to fragment $= 4500 - 20 = 4480$ bytes. With $\text{MTU} = 600$, maximum payload per fragment must be a multiple of 8: $\lfloor (600 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 72 \times 8 = 576$ bytes. Fragment 1 carries bytes 0 to 575 (offset 0). Fragment 2 carries bytes 576 to 1151 (offset $576/8 = 72$). Fragment 3 carries bytes 1152 onwards, so its fragment offset field is $\frac{1152}{8} = 144$.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider an IP packet with a length of 4,500 bytes that includes a 20-byte IPv4 header and a 40-byte TCP header. The packet is forwarded across an IP network with an MTU of 600 bytes. The value of the fragment offset field in the third fragment (in 8-byte units) is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

questions.question_text:
Consider an enterprise network with two Ethernet segments, a web server and a
firewall, connected via three routers as shown below.
What is the number of subnets inside the enterprise network?

options.D:
8
Q.23 – Q.27 Multiple Select Questions (MSQ), carry ONE mark each.

questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: In the enterprise topology, subnets are formed by distinct broadcast domains separated by router interfaces: 2 Ethernet LAN segments (2 subnets), 1 web server subnet (1 subnet), 1 internal firewall segment (1 subnet), and 2 point-to-point links between the routers (2 subnets), yielding a total of 6 subnets.

resolver. Assume that no resource records are cached anywhere across the DNS

questions.question_text:
Consider a 100 Mbps link between an earth station (sender) and a satellite (receiver)
at an altitude of 2100 km. The signal propagates at a speed of 3x108 m/s. The time
taken (in milliseconds, rounded off to two decimal places) for the receiver to
completely receive a packet of 1000 bytes transmitted by the sender is_________.
questions.subtopic: Data link layer: framing, error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet bridging
questions.explaination: Propagation time is $T_{\text{prop}} = \frac{2100 \times 10^3\text{ m}}{3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}} = 7.00\text{ ms}$. Transmission time is $T_{\text{trans}} = \frac{1000 \times 8\text{ bits}}{100 \times 10^6\text{ bps}} = 0.08\text{ ms}$. Total time to completely receive the packet is $T_{\text{prop}} + T_{\text{trans}} = 7.00 + 0.08 = 7.08\text{ ms}$.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a 100 Mbps link between an earth station (sender) and a satellite (receiver) at an altitude of 2100 km. The signal propagates at a speed of $3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$. The time taken (in milliseconds, rounded off to two decimal places) for the receiver to completely receive a packet of 1000 bytes transmitted by the sender is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in numeric format)

questions.question_text:
Consider the data transfer using TCP over a 1 Gbps link. Assuming that the
maximum segment lifetime (MSL) is set to 60 seconds, the minimum number of
bits required for the sequence number field of the TCP header, to prevent the
sequence number space from wrapping around during the MSL is____________.
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: Data transmitted at 1 Gbps line rate in $\text{MSL} = 60\text{ s}$ is $\frac{10^9\text{ bps}}{8} \times 60\text{ s} = 7.5 \times 10^9\text{ bytes}$. The sequence number space must satisfy $2^k \ge 7.5 \times 10^9$. Since $2^{32} \approx 4.29 \times 10^9 < 7.5 \times 10^9$ and $2^{33} \approx 8.59 \times 10^9 > 7.5 \times 10^9$, at least 33 bits are required.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider the data transfer using TCP over a 1 Gbps link. Assuming that the maximum segment lifetime (MSL) is set to 60 seconds, the minimum number of bits required for the sequence number field of the TCP header, to prevent the sequence number space from wrapping around during the MSL is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

questions.question_text:
Suppose two hosts are connected by a point-to-point link and they are conﬁgured
to use Stop-and-Wait protocol for reliable data transfer. Identify in which one of
the following scenarios, the utilization of the link is the lowest.

options.A: Longer link length and lower transmission rate
options.B: Longer link length and higher transmission rate
options.C: Shorter link length and lower transmission rate
options.D:
Shorter link length and higher transmission rate
CS

questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: Link utilization in Stop-and-Wait is $\eta = \frac{1}{1 + 2a}$, where $a = \frac{T_{\text{prop}}}{T_{\text{trans}}} = \frac{d/v}{L/B} = \frac{d \cdot B}{v \cdot L}$. Utilization $\eta$ is lowest when parameter $a$ is maximized, which occurs when the link length $d$ is longer (increasing propagation delay) and the transmission rate $B$ is higher (decreasing packet transmission time).
questions.question_text_latex: Suppose two hosts are connected by a point-to-point link and they are configured to use Stop-and-Wait protocol for reliable data transfer. Identify in which one of the following scenarios, the utilization of the link is the lowest.

options_latex.A: Longer link length and lower transmission rate
options_latex.B: Longer link length and higher transmission rate
options_latex.C: Shorter link length and lower transmission rate
options_latex.D: Shorter link length and higher transmission rate

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about
the OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocol used in the Internet?

options.A: OSPF implements Bellman-Ford algorithm to ﬁnd shortest paths.
options.B: OSPF uses Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm to implement least-cost path routing.
options.C: OSPF is used as an inter-domain routing protocol.

questions.subtopic: Routing protocols: shortest path, flooding, distance vector and link state routing
questions.explaination: OSPF is an intra-domain (Interior Gateway) routing protocol that uses Dijkstra's link-state algorithm (not Bellman-Ford, which is used by distance-vector protocols like RIP). Therefore, statement A (implements Bellman-Ford) and statement C (used as inter-domain) are INCORRECT, which are the required answers.
questions.question_text_latex: Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about the OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocol used in the Internet?

options_latex.A: OSPF implements Bellman-Ford algorithm to find shortest paths.
options_latex.B: OSPF uses Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm to implement least-cost path routing.
options_latex.C: OSPF is used as an inter-domain routing protocol.

questions.question_text:
Suppose you are asked to design a new reliable byte-stream transport protocol
like TCP. This protocol, named myTCP, runs over a 100 Mbps network with Round
Trip Time of 150 milliseconds and the maximum segment lifetime of 2 minutes.
Which of the following is/are valid lengths of the Sequence Number ﬁeld in the
myTCP header?
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: To prevent sequence number wraparound within the Maximum Segment Lifetime ($MSL = 2\text{ min} = 120\text{ s}$), the sequence number space $2^k$ must be at least the data bytes transmitted at line rate during MSL: $2^k \ge \frac{100 \times 10^6\text{ bps}}{8} \times 120\text{ s} = 1.5 \times 10^9\text{ bytes}$. Since $2^{30} \approx 1.07 \times 10^9 < 1.5 \times 10^9$ and $2^{31} \approx 2.15 \times 10^9 > 1.5 \times 10^9$, at least 31 bits are required. Thus, 32 bits, 34 bits, and 36 bits are all valid lengths.

Suppose you are asked to design a new reliable byte-stream transport protocol like TCP. This protocol, named myTCP, runs over a 100 Mbps network with Round Trip Time of 150 milliseconds and the maximum segment lifetime of 2 minutes.

questions.question_text:
Suppose in a web browser, you click on the www.gate-2023.in URL. The browser
cache is empty. The IP address for this URL is not cached in your local host, so
a DNS lookup is triggered (by the local DNS server deployed on your local host)
over the 3-tier DNS hierarchy in an iterative mode. No resource records are cached
anywhere across all DNS servers.
Let RTT denote the round trip time between your local host and DNS servers
in the DNS hierarchy. The round trip time between the local host and the web
server hosting www.gate-2023.in is also equal to RTT. The HTML ﬁle associated
with the URL is small enough to have negligible transmission time and negligible
rendering time by your web browser, which references 10 equally small objects on
the same web server.
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT about the minimum elapsed
time between clicking on the URL and your browser fully rendering it?

options.A: 7 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.
options.B: 5 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
options.C: 9 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.
options.D:
6 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
CS

questions.subtopic: Application layer protocols: DNS, SMTP, HTTP, FTP, Email
questions.explaination: Resolving the URL via 3-tier iterative DNS requires $3\text{ RTT}$. Initiating TCP connection and requesting the base HTML page requires $1 + 1 = 2\text{ RTT}$, so the base HTML is received after $3 + 2 = 5\text{ RTT}$. With persistent HTTP pipelining, all 10 objects are fetched in 1 round trip over the established connection, giving $5 + 1 = 6\text{ RTT}$ (D is TRUE). With non-persistent HTTP and 5 parallel connections, fetching 10 objects takes 2 sequential batches; each batch takes $1\text{ RTT (TCP)} + 1\text{ RTT (HTTP)} = 2\text{ RTT}$, adding $2 \times 2 = 4\text{ RTT}$, giving $5 + 4 = 9\text{ RTT}$ (C is TRUE).

Suppose in a web browser, you click on the `www.gate-2023.in` URL. The browser cache is empty. questions.question_text:
A user starts browsing a webpage hosted at a remote server. The browser opens a
single TCP connection to fetch the entire webpage from the server. The webpage
consists of a top-level index page with multiple embedded image objects. Assume
that all caches (e.g., DNS cache, browser cache) are all initially empty. The
following packets leave the user’s computer in some order.
(i)
HTTP GET request for the index page
(ii)
DNS request to resolve the web server’s name to its IP address
(iii)
HTTP GET request for an image object
(iv)
TCP SYN to open a connection to the web server
Which one of the following is the CORRECT chronological order (earliest in time
to latest) of the packets leaving the computer ?
questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: Initially all caches are empty. The client must first send a DNS query (ii) to resolve the server hostname to an IP. Next, it establishes a TCP connection by sending TCP SYN (iv). Once connected, it sends an HTTP GET request for the index HTML page (i). After parsing the HTML and identifying embedded images, it sends HTTP GET requests for the images (iii).

questions.question_text:
TCP client P successfully establishes a connection to TCP server Q. Let 𝑁𝑃 denote
the sequence number in the SYN sent from P to Q. Let 𝑁𝑄 denote the
acknowledgement number in the SYN ACK from Q to P. Which of the following
statements is/are CORRECT?

options.A: The sequence number 𝑁𝑃 is chosen randomly by P
options.B: The sequence number 𝑁𝑃 is always 0 for a new connection
options.C: The acknowledgement number 𝑁𝑄 is equal to 𝑁𝑃
options.D: The acknowledgement number 𝑁𝑄 is equal to 𝑁𝑃+ 1

questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: During TCP connection establishment, the initial sequence number $N_P$ is chosen pseudo-randomly to avoid cross-connection packet collisions and mitigate spoofing attacks (A is TRUE). Because a SYN packet consumes exactly 1 sequence number in the sequence space, server $Q$ acknowledges it with $N_Q = N_P + 1$ (D is TRUE).
questions.question_text_latex: TCP client P successfully establishes a connection to TCP server Q. Let $N_P$ denote the sequence number in the SYN sent from P to Q. Let $N_Q$ denote the acknowledgement number in the SYN ACK from Q to P. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

options_latex.A: The sequence number $N_P$ is chosen randomly by P
options_latex.B: The sequence number $N_P$ is always 0 for a new connection
options_latex.C: The acknowledgement number $N_Q$ is equal to $N_P$
options_latex.D: The acknowledgement number $N_Q$ is equal to $N_P + 1$

Which of the following fields is/are modified in the IP header of a packet going out
of a network address translation (NAT) device from an internal network to an
external network?
questions.subtopic: Network Address Translation (NAT)
questions.explaination: When a packet leaves a private subnet through an outbound NAT gateway, the router rewrites the private Source IP address to its public external IP address (A is modified). Because the IP header fields have changed, the IPv4 Header Checksum must be recalculated and replaced (C is modified). Destination IP and Total Length are unmodified.

questions.question_text:
Consider a network path P—Q—R between nodes P and R via router Q. Node P
sends a file of size 106 bytes to R via this path by splitting the file into chunks of
103 bytes each. Node P sends these chunks one after the other without any wait time
between the successive chunk transmissions. Assume that the size of extra headers
added to these chunks is negligible, and that the chunk size is less than the MTU.

Each of the links P—Q and Q—R has a bandwidth of 106 bits/sec, and negligible
propagation latency. Router Q immediately transmits every packet it receives from
P to R, with negligible processing and queueing delays. Router Q can
simultaneously receive on link P—Q and transmit on link Q—R.

Assume P starts transmitting the chunks at time 𝑡= 0.
Which one of the following options gives the time (in seconds, rounded off to 3
decimal places) at which R receives all the chunks of the file?
questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: The file size is $10^6$ bytes split into 1000 chunks of $10^3$ bytes ($8000$ bits) each. Link transmission time for one chunk is $\frac{8000\text{ bits}}{10^6\text{ bps}} = 0.008\text{ s}$. Node P completes sending all 1000 chunks at $t = 1000 \times 0.008 = 8.000\text{ s}$. The last chunk arrives at router Q at $t = 8.000\text{ s}$ and takes another $0.008\text{ s}$ to reach R over link Q---R, completing at $8.008\text{ s}$.

Assume P starts transmitting the chunks at time $t = 0$.
Which one of the following options gives the time (in seconds, rounded off to 3 decimal places) at which R receives all the chunks of the file?

questions.question_text:
Consider sending an IP datagram of size 1420 bytes (including 20 bytes of IP
header) from a sender to a receiver over a path of two links with a router between
them. The first link (sender to router) has an MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit)
size of 542 bytes, while the second link (router to receiver) has an MTU size of 360
bytes. The number of fragments that would be delivered at the receiver is ________
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: The datagram has 20 bytes IP header and 1400 bytes data. Link 1 has $\text{MTU} = 542$ bytes (max data per fragment is $\lfloor (542-20)/8 \rfloor \times 8 = 520$ bytes), producing 3 fragments with data sizes 520, 520, and 360 bytes. Link 2 has $\text{MTU} = 360$ bytes (max data is $\lfloor (360-20)/8 \rfloor \times 8 = 336$ bytes). At router Q, fragment 1 (520 bytes) is fragmented into 2 ($336 + 184$), fragment 2 (520 bytes) is fragmented into 2 ($336 + 184$), and fragment 3 (360 bytes) is fragmented into 2 ($336 + 24$). Total fragments delivered at the receiver $= 2 + 2 + 2 = 6$.

The first link (sender to router) has an MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) size of 542 bytes, while the second link (router to receiver) has an MTU size of 360 bytes. The number of fragments that would be delivered at the receiver is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

Node X has a TCP connection open to node Y. The packets from X to Y go through
an intermediate IP router R. Ethernet switch S is the first switch on the network path
between X and R. Consider a packet sent from X to Y over this connection.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the destination IP and MAC
addresses on this packet at the time it leaves X?

options.A: The destination IP address is the IP address of R
options.B: The destination IP address is the IP address of Y
options.C: The destination MAC address is the MAC address of S
options.D: The destination MAC address is the MAC address of Y

questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: In an end-to-end IP network, the destination IP address remains invariant throughout transit and is always the IP address of final host Y. The destination MAC address changes hop-by-hop and is set to the MAC address of the next-hop router R (not switch S, which operates transparently at Layer 2).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation is/are TRUE?

options.A:
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed only at the source of the
datagram
options.B:
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed at any IP router which finds
that the size of the datagram to be transmitted exceeds the MTU
options.C: The reassembly of fragments is performed only at the destination of the datagram
options.D:
The reassembly of fragments is performed at all intermediate routers along the
path from the source to the destination

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: In IPv4, any intermediate router encountering a packet larger than the outgoing link MTU performs fragmentation (B). In contrast, fragment reassembly is performed strictly at the final destination host (C) to prevent re-fragmentation overhead and handle out-of-order routing.

Which of the following fields of an IP header is/are always modified by any router
before it forwards the IP packet?
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: Whenever an IP packet is processed by an intermediate router, its Time to Live (TTL) field is decremented by at least 1. Because the header content changes, the router must recompute and update the Header Checksum field. Source and Protocol remain unchanged.

questions.question_text:
Which one of the following CIDR prefixes exactly represents the range of
IP addresses 10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255?
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: The address range spans from $10.12.2.0$ ($00000010_2$) to $10.12.3.255$ ($00000011_2$). The first 23 bits ($8 + 8 + 7 = 23$) are identical ($10.12.2$). Total addresses in range $= 2 \times 256 = 512 = 2^{32 - 23}$, which exactly matches CIDR prefix `10.12.2.0/23`.

questions.question_text:
Consider a TCP connection operating at a point of time with the congestion window
of size 12 MSS (Maximum Segment Size), when a timeout occurs due to packet
loss. Assuming that all the segments transmitted in the next two RTTs (Round Trip
Time) are acknowledged correctly, the congestion window size (in MSS) during the
third RTT will be _________
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: When timeout occurs at $\text{cwnd} = 12\text{ MSS}$, slow start threshold is set to $\text{ssthresh} = \lfloor 12 / 2 \rfloor = 6\text{ MSS}$, and $\text{cwnd}$ resets to $1\text{ MSS}$ for the 1st RTT. After receiving ACKs in the 1st RTT, slow start doubles $\text{cwnd}$ to $2\text{ MSS}$ during the 2nd RTT. After receiving ACKs in the 2nd RTT, $\text{cwnd}$ doubles again to $4\text{ MSS}$ during the 3rd RTT.

questions.question_text:
Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of 108 bits/sec and a
maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal
in the medium is 2×108 meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required
for collision detection is _________
questions.subtopic: Data link layer: framing, error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet bridging
questions.explaination: Propagation delay $T_p = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Velocity}} = \frac{500}{2 \times 10^8} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s} = 2.5\,\mu\text{s}$. For collision detection in CSMA/CD, transmission time must satisfy $T_t \ge 2 T_p = 5\,\mu\text{s}$. Minimum frame size $L = 2 T_p \times B = (5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}) \times 10^8\text{ bps} = 500$ bits.

Consider the 3-way handshaking protocol for TCP connection establishment. Let
the three packets exchanged during the connection establishment be denoted as P1,
P2, and P3, in order. Which of the following option(s) is/are TRUE with respect to
TCP header flags that are set in the packets?

options.D:
P1: SYN = 1

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: In TCP 3-way handshaking: Packet 1 (Client to Server) sends a SYN segment with flag $[\text{SYN}=1, \text{ACK}=0]$; Packet 2 (Server to Client) responds with $[\text{SYN}=1, \text{ACK}=1]$; Packet 3 (Client to Server) completes setup with $[\text{SYN}=0, \text{ACK}=1]$. Hence, P1 has SYN = 1 and P2 has SYN = 1, ACK = 1.

questions.question_text:
A packet with the destination IP address 145.36.109.70 arrives at a router whose
routing table is shown. Which interface will the packet be forwarded to?
questions.subtopic: Routing protocols: shortest path, flooding, distance vector and link state routing
questions.explaination: The destination address has third octet $109 = 01101101_2$. For /16, $145.36.0.0$ matches. For /17 ($128 = 10000000_2$), the leading bit is 0, so /17 does not match. For /18 ($64 = 01000000_2$), the first two bits are $01_2$, which matches $109$ ($01101101_2$). For /24, 255 does not match. By Longest Prefix Match, /18 (interface E3) is chosen.

questions.question_text:
Suppose a 5-bit message is transmitted from a source to a destination through a
noisy channel. The probability that a bit of the message gets flipped during
transmission is 0.01. Flipping of each bit is independent of one another. The
probability that the message is delivered error-free to the destination is ______ .
(rounded off to three decimal places)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Data link layer: framing, error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet bridging
questions.explaination: For each bit, the probability of correct transmission without flipping is $1 - 0.01 = 0.99$. Since all 5 bit transmissions are mutually independent, the probability that all 5 bits are transmitted error-free is $(0.99)^5 = 0.95099 \approx 0.951$.

questions.question_text:
Suppose a message of size 15000 bytes is transmitted from a source to a destination
using IPv4 protocol via two routers as shown in the figure. Each router has a defined
maximum transmission unit (MTU) as shown in the figure, including IP header.
The number of fragments that will be delivered to the destination is ________ .
(Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: At Router-1, max payload per fragment is $\lfloor (5000 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 4976$ bytes. 15000 bytes payload is fragmented into payloads of 4976, 4976, 4976, and 72 bytes (4 fragments). At Router-2 ($\text{MTU} = 3000$, max payload $\lfloor 2980/8 \rfloor \times 8 = 2976$ bytes), each of the three 4976-byte fragments splits into 2 fragments ($2976 + 2000$), yielding $3 \times 2 = 6$ fragments. The 72-byte fragment passes through intact. Total delivered fragments = $6 + 1 = 7$.

A machine receives an IPv4 datagram. The protocol field of the IPv4 header has the

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: The IPv4 Protocol field identifies the payload carried directly in the IP datagram: ICMP (protocol 1), IGMP (protocol 2), and OSPF (protocol 89). In contrast, RIP runs as an application-layer process encapsulated inside UDP (port 520).

questions.question_text:
Consider a network that uses Ethernet and IPv4. Assume that IPv4 headers do not
use any options field. Each Ethernet frame can carry a maximum of 1500 bytes in
its data field. A UDP segment is transmitted. The payload (data) in the UDP
segment is 7488 bytes.
Which ONE of the following choices has the CORRECT total number of fragments
transmitted and the size of the last fragment including IPv4 header?
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing
questions.explaination: UDP payload is 7488 bytes + 8 bytes UDP header = 7496 bytes IP payload. Max IP payload per Ethernet fragment is $\lfloor(1500 - 20)/8\rfloor \times 8 = 1480$ bytes. Fragment sizes are 5 fragments of 1480 bytes ($5 \times 1480 = 7400$), leaving $7496 - 7400 = 96$ bytes for the 6th fragment, so total size is $96 + 20 = 116$ bytes.

questions.question_text:
Suppose we are transmitting frames between two nodes using Stop-and-Wait
protocol. The frame size is 3000 bits. The transmission rate of the channel is 2000
bps (bits/second) and the propagation delay between the two nodes is 100
milliseconds. Assume that the processing times at the source and destination are
negligible. Also, assume that the size of the acknowledgement packet is negligible.
Which ONE of the following most accurately gives the channel utilization for the
above scenario in percentage?
questions.subtopic: Data link layer: flow control and Stop-and-Wait efficiency
questions.explaination: Efficiency in Stop-and-Wait is $\eta = \frac{T_t}{T_t + 2 T_p}$. Substituting given transmission and propagation delays yields $\eta = 88.23\%$.
